title: bug: Windows PowerShell 5.1 seats get a mojibake stable role prefix (Get-RoleDoc reads the BOM-less UTF-8 role doc as ANSI)
description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1 Get-RoleDoc reads .moe/roles/<role>.md with `Get-Content -Raw -Path $p` and no -Encoding. The daemon writes role docs as BOM-less UTF-8, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the JetBrains plugin's native Windows engine) decodes a BOM-less file as ANSI, so every em dash, arrow and comparison sign in the stable system prefix ($systemAppend: the Claude system prompt file and the codex/gemini/grok instruction files) arrives garbled.
Repro (architect-e4b7eee0, 2026-10-29, PowerShell 5.1.26100 via powershell.exe): on a copy of .moe/roles/worker.md, the default read contains no U+2014 and does contain U+00E2 (mojibake); `Get-Content -Raw -Encoding UTF8` reads the em dash correctly. pwsh 7 is unaffected (UTF-8 default). The bash twin (`cat`) is unaffected.
Fix: read with `-Encoding UTF8` (correct on 5.1 and 7, BOM or not) and pin it with a launcher regression on both PowerShell engines that renders the real Get-RoleDoc + $systemAppend assembly against a BOM-less UTF-8 role doc containing non-ASCII text. Found while planning CQ-C10 (task-34632f08), whose stable-prefix test needs the exact role doc on every engine.
definitionOfDone: Get-RoleDoc in scripts/moe-agent.ps1 reads the role doc as UTF-8 on both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7, so $systemAppend carries the doc's exact non-ASCII text (em dash, arrows, comparison signs).

A launcher regression in scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs runs the real Get-RoleDoc and $systemAppend assembly on powershell.exe and pwsh against a BOM-less UTF-8 role doc. It fails on the old read and passes on the fix, with the red result recorded.
No other ps1 read path or bash behavior changes, and `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` still exits 0.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs` run on Windows (both PowerShell engines plus Git Bash) exits 0, and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Keep scripts/moe-agent.ps1 saved as UTF-8 with a BOM and in string parity with scripts/moe-agent.sh.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

Edit the LANDED bytes. Three dependencies edit scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and land first: ad0dc2e7, bc8410af and c2a900aa. Re-read Get-RoleDoc (around line 659) and the stable-prefix assembly (`$roleDoc = Get-RoleDoc` / `$systemAppend = $systemAppendPre`, around line 6227) before editing.

In scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs, add a test after the `const psEngines = ...` line. It needs psEngines, so it must come after that definition. Mirror the ParseFile test's skip: if (!psEngines.length), register a skipped test 'Get-RoleDoc reads the UTF-8 role doc on PowerShell 5.1 and 7' with `no PowerShell engine on ${process.platform}`. Then, for each engine of psEngines, add test `${engine}: Get-RoleDoc puts the exact UTF-8 role doc in the stable system prefix`:
- ROLE_DOC_TEXT = '# Worker — role
A → B ← C, x ≤ y ≥ z, «q» 漢字
'. Use escapes in the test source so the test file stays ASCII.
- Run two cases, one per bom in [false, true]:
  - In a fresh mkdtemp dir (removed in t.after), write roles/worker.md as Buffer.concat([bom ? Buffer.from([0xef, 0xbb, 0xbf]) : Buffer.alloc(0), Buffer.from(ROLE_DOC_TEXT, 'utf8')]).
  - Build script = '﻿' + "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$moeDir=$env:MOE_TEST_DIR
$Role='worker'
$pluginRoot=$null
$systemAppendPre='stable prefix'
" + between(read('ps1'), 'function Get-RoleDoc {', '
$roleDoc = Get-RoleDoc') + '
' + between(read('ps1'), '    $roleDoc = Get-RoleDoc
    $systemAppend = $systemAppendPre', '    $dynamicContext = ""') + "
[IO.File]::WriteAllText($env:MOE_TEST_OUT, $systemAppend, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding $false))".
    This runs the REAL function and the REAL assembly. The result is written as UTF-8 to a file, never to stdout: PowerShell 5.1's redirected stdout would transcode it and confound the check.
  - spawnSync(engine, ['-NoProfile', '-File', file]) with env MOE_TEST_DIR=dir and MOE_TEST_OUT=<dir>/out.txt. Status must be 0, and readFileSync(out, 'utf8') must equal 'stable prefix

' + ROLE_DOC_TEXT exactly, with no U+FEFF and no U+00E2.

RED, recorded in the step note: run the new test with Windows Node on a copy of scripts/ (step 3's recipe) against the UNFIXED moe-agent.ps1. powershell.exe must FAIL the bom=false case with mojibake (U+00E2 instead of U+2014). pwsh.exe passes, because its default is UTF-8. Keep that failure output.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1, Get-RoleDoc: change `if (Test-Path $p) { return Get-Content -Raw -Path $p }` to `if (Test-Path $p) { return Get-Content -Raw -Encoding UTF8 -Path $p }`.

Add a one-line comment above it: the daemon writes role docs as BOM-less UTF-8; Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes a BOM-less file as ANSI unless told; -Encoding UTF8 is correct on 5.1 and 7, BOM or not.

Nothing else changes:
- no other Get-Content call;
- no bash change, since `cat` is byte-exact;
- no parity strings.
Use an exact-string edit. Keep the file's UTF-8 BOM (ef bb bf) and its LF line endings: no CRLF conversion and no re-encoding. Confirm with `head -c 3 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | od -An -tx1` and `grep -c $'\r$' scripts/moe-agent.ps1` (0).

Error handling: unchanged. A missing doc still returns "". -Encoding UTF8 never throws on invalid bytes; it substitutes U+FFFD, the same failure class as before, now with the correct decoding for valid files.
implementationPlan.note: Get-RoleDoc now reads with -Encoding UTF8 plus one comment line. BOM (ef bb bf) kept, 0 CR lines, diff is +2/-1 in the file.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected alternatives:
- [IO.File]::ReadAllText(path), which defaults to UTF-8 with BOM detection. It would also work, but `Get-Content -Raw -Encoding UTF8` is the smallest change, matches the task's stated fix, and is correct on 5.1 and 7.
- Changing other Get-Content reads, for example of JSON. Out of scope by DoD 3: those are ConvertFrom-Json of ASCII-escaped daemon JSON, or separate issues.
- Comparing stdout. PowerShell 5.1 transcodes redirected stdout through the console code page, so the test writes the result to a file as UTF-8.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Get-RoleDoc is at around moe-agent.ps1:659. The stable prefix is assembled at around 6227-6231: $systemAppend = $systemAppendPre + "`n`n$roleDoc". It reaches claude's system prompt file and the codex, gemini and grok instruction files.

The test helper read() normalizes CRLF; between(source, start, end) takes the first end after start. On win32, engines = powershell.exe, pwsh.exe and Git Bash; psEngines is defined at around line 460, just before the ParseFile test, whose skip pattern the new test mirrors.

moe-agent.ps1 has a UTF-8 BOM and LF endings (autocrlf=false). .moe/roles/worker.md is BOM-less UTF-8 containing em dashes and arrows. The bash twin's load_role_doc uses $(cat), which is byte-exact apart from trailing newlines; that is pre-existing and out of scope.

completionSummary:
Get-RoleDoc in scripts/moe-agent.ps1 now reads with -Encoding UTF8, so Windows PowerShell 5.1 no longer decodes the daemon's BOM-less UTF-8 role doc as ANSI. The change is +2/-1 (one comment line plus the read). The file keeps its BOM and LF endings. No bash change.
Test: prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs gains a block that runs the real Get-RoleDoc and the real $systemAppend assembly on powershell.exe and pwsh.exe, for a BOM-less and a BOM'd role doc. The role doc contains an em dash, arrows, comparison signs, guillemets and CJK. The result is written to a file as UTF-8 and compared exactly, so there is no stdout transcoding confound.
RED, recorded before the fix on Windows Node against a temp copy: only powershell.exe BOM-less failed, at the no-mojibake assertion. powershell.exe with BOM and both pwsh.exe cases passed.
GREEN after the fix: 96/96 pass on Windows, 0 skipped. parity-check.sh passes. On Linux the new test is skipped with 'no PowerShell engine on linux'.
